definition: In machine learning, automatic basis function construction, also known as basis discovery, is a technique that finds a set of general-purpose (task-independent) basis functions to simplify complex data (state space) into a smaller, manageable form (lower-dimensional embedding) while accurately capturing the value function.
details: Unlike methods relying on expert-designed functions, this approach works without prior knowledge of the specific problem area (domain), making it effective in situations where creating tailored basis functions is challenging or impractical.

explainer.lead: Automatic basis function construction is a way to learn a compact set of features for representing complex states. It aims to make value-function approximation manageable without requiring someone to hand-design features for the particular problem.

tiers.eli5: Imagine describing every place in a huge maze by writing down lots of tiny details. This approach learns a shorter set of useful descriptions on its own, so the maze becomes easier to work with while keeping the information needed to judge how good each place is.
tiers.practitioner: Use it when approximating a value function over a large state space and hand-crafted basis functions are difficult or impractical to design. The goal is a lower-dimensional embedding that still represents the value function accurately, rather than simply making the state vector smaller.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a state space S, basis discovery seeks task-independent basis functions whose span provides a lower-dimensional representation of states while accurately capturing the value function. Its distinguishing requirement is construction without domain-specific prior knowledge; reducing dimension alone is insufficient if value information is lost.

explainer.example: For a maze whose states contain many detailed measurements, basis discovery might learn a small set of features that represents each location with only a few numbers. A value-function approximator can then work with that compact description instead of the full measurements, provided the learned basis preserves the value information.

usedIn.detail: Represents complex states with learned basis functions for value-function approximation.

usedIn.name: High-dimensional state representation
usedIn.detail: Produces a lower-dimensional embedding that is easier to manage than the original state space.

explainer.intuition: A small, well-chosen set of building blocks can describe a complicated state more compactly than the raw representation. Basis discovery learns those building blocks itself, aiming for general-purpose features that preserve what matters for the value function.
howItWorks: Start with states from a complex or high-dimensional state space.
Construct candidate basis functions without relying on expert-designed, domain-specific features.
Select a general-purpose set of basis functions for representing states.
Express each state in a lower-dimensional embedding.
Check that the compact representation still accurately captures the value function.
explainer.whyItMatters: It removes much of the burden of designing basis functions by hand, which can be difficult when the problem domain is poorly understood or the state space is complex. A good learned basis makes value-function approximation more manageable without sacrificing the information the approximation needs.
misconceptions: It is not just any dimensionality-reduction method: the representation must also capture the value function accurately.
Task-independent does not mean value information can be ignored; the basis is general-purpose but still supports value-function approximation.
It does not depend on experts supplying tailored features for the specific domain.
